subject: Control path surge observed in Cardinal Health VPC — remediation and artifacts
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Miller <devon@cardinalhealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: [Action Required] Control path surge observed in Cardinal Health VPC — immediate mitigation and artifacts

Hi Devon —

Quick update from the morning: between 08:45–09:10 PDT our telemetry showed a sudden spike of control-plane connection retries originating from the Cardinal Health private deployment. Symptoms were: elevated orchestration RPC latency, repeated agent reconnections, and several short-lived request failures (5xx) for private model endpoints.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled back the agent rollout to 2.3.0 for the affected pool at 09:00 PDT (we observed stabilization within ~6min).
- Enabled extended tracing and collected live controlplane traces and agent logs.
- Opened a dedicated incident channel and notified engineering on-call.

Preliminary impact: ~18 minutes of elevated error rates for a subset of pods; customers routed to the Dedicated fallback experienced no interruption. We did not see data plane data leakage.

Attachments: controlplane-trace-20280706.json, vm-logs-20280706.tar.gz (redwood debug bundle).

Next steps we propose — please confirm you’re OK with us sharing these artifacts with your networking team and running a short NAT/port-listing check from a customer-side bastion (we will coordinate and keep any sensitive outputs limited to debug bundles).

If you’d like a 30-minute bridge to walk through traces, we can schedule within the hour. We’ll follow up with a root-cause summary and remediation plan by EOD PST.

Thanks and apologies for the disruption — we’ll own the follow-up.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Devon Miller <devon@cardinalhealth.ai>

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the quick rollback and the heads up.

Please go ahead and share the artifacts with our networking team (ops@cardinalhealth.ai). We need:
- A short timeline of events we can share internally.
- Any indications that the issue increased outbound NAT consumption on our side (we’ve seen port exhaustion before in similar setups).
- ETA for a postmortem and whether a credit review is going to be initiated (we’ll need this for our procurement team).

We are available for a bridge at 10:00 PDT if that helps.

—Devon
Director, Platform Reliability
Cardinal Health AI

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Jul 2028 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Cardinal Health control-path spike — hypothesis and next actions

Aditya / Laura — internal notes and asks (do not forward outside the company).

What we observed:
- Spike correlated with agent rollout to version 2.3.1 at 08:38 PDT for one AZ pool.
- Control-plane logs show repeated TLS renegotiation attempts and then half-closed sessions; concurrent connection counts briefly doubled for the pool.
- The customer’s network team reported transient NAT port scarcity in their logs during the same timeframe (Devon copied ops).

Hypothesis: a TLS renegotiation edge-case introduced in 2.3.1 causes agents to open additional ephemeral control connections under load; on customer NATs with limited ephemeral ports this leads to connection churn and RPC backpressure.

Asks:
- Aditya: please prioritize producing a focused RCA artifact (controlplane traces annotated, stack traces, and a minimal repro if possible) and a patch candidate to avoid the renegotiation path. Target: first pass patch and test harness by Monday EOD.
- Laura: coordinate the customer communications cadence, confirm bridge scheduling for 10:00 PDT, and prepare a short credit/impact estimate for commercial to review.

I’ll prepare the incident timeline and upload artifacts to the shared drive (link below).

—Naomi

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Devon Miller <devon@cardinalhealth.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Cardinal Health VPC — incident summary, root cause, and remediation plan

Hi Devon / SaaSOps team —

Thanks for the bridge and patience over the weekend. Below is the consolidated post-incident summary and next steps.

Incident summary (timeline):
- 08:38 PDT Fri 2028-07-06: Agent rollout to v2.3.1 started for pool in us-west-2 AZ-b.
- 08:45–09:03 PDT: Increase in control-plane TLS handshake retries and agent reconnections; customer-side NAT port reports show ephemeral port reuse warnings at 08:50.
- 09:00 PDT: We rolled back the pool to agent v2.3.0. Error rates subsided by ~09:06.

Root cause (short):
- A regression in agent v2.3.1 introduces an unnecessary TLS renegotiation on reconnection attempts under certain keepalive timing windows. That behavior multiplied concurrent control connections for affected hosts and, combined with limited customer ephemeral ports, caused connection churn and RPC timeouts.

Corrective and preventive actions:
- Immediate: rollback completed (done) and extended monitoring remains in place.
- Short-term (this week): patch the agent to eliminate forced renegotiation and add an exponential backoff for reconnect attempts (owner: Aditya Rao; ETA: 2028-07-11 EOD).
- Mid-term: test harness to simulate customer NAT constraints and a canary rollout plan (owner: Aditya Rao; ETA: 2028-07-18).
- Preventive: update our upgrade checklist to include ephemeral-port-sensitivity tests for private deployments (owner: Engineering Release PM; ETA: 2028-07-25).

Artifacts we’ve attached/shared: controlplane-trace-20280706.json (annotated), vm-logs-20280706.tar.gz, remediation-playbook-v1.md. Full evidence and trace links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Cardinal-Health-Incident-20280706

Commercial notes: Laura will coordinate a credit assessment and next steps with your procurement team. We will proactively create a postmortem doc and circulate a final timeline once the patch is validated in our staging harness.

Please let me know if you’d like anything added to the remediation playbook or if your networking team wants deeper packet-level captures (we can schedule a narrow window for that).

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority and will keep you updated on progress toward the patch and canary.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
